title: Resource Entitlement and Vendor Onsite Procedures (Comprehensive Playbook)
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines company-wide procedures for resource entitlement (access & permissions), change management gates, data handling expectations, procurement & expense approvals, vendor onboarding and onsite procedures, and travel approvals. It is intended for requesters, approvers, IT operations, security, procurement, and people managers.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single operational reference for cross-functional approvals and controls that balance speed and risk.
- Applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors requiring access to Redwood resources, requests for purchases, travel, and requests to bring vendors onsite/into our network.
- Excludes tactical team-level procedures where a specific team maintains stricter controls (these must link back to this playbook).

Definitions:
1) Entitlement: any identity or system permission granting access to compute, data, or corporate services.
2) Vendor Onsite: third-party personnel physically present at Redwood offices or using company-managed jump hosts/VPN.
3) Emergency Change: a non-routine change that must be applied outside normal CAB cadence to avoid operational degradation.
4) Sensitive Data: regulated, PII/PHI, or any dataset classified as Confidential or higher.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Requester: initiates requests in the Service Portal with business rationale and scope.
- Approver: assigned manager or product owner who verifies business need.
- IAM Owner (IT): validates least-privilege mapping, group membership, and SSO provisioning steps.
- Security Reviewer: reviews requests for access to Sensitive Data or network segmentation exceptions.
- Procurement Lead: validates PR thresholds, vendor contracts, and PO issuance.
- Facilities/Front Desk: coordinates onsite logistics and badge/escort requirements for vendors.

Approval matrix (summary):
| Request Type | Typical Approver | Security Review Required | Procurement Threshold | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Standard SaaS subscription (<= $25k/year) | Line Manager | No | Auto-approve via procurement punchout | Use approved vendor list |
| Hardware or Dedicated GPU nodes (one-off > $25k) | Engineering Manager + Infra Lead | Yes | Requires PO and Contract Review | Finance sign-off required |
| Access to Confidential data set | Data Owner + Security Reviewer | Yes | n/a | Provisional 30-day access by default |
| Vendor Onsite with network access | Procurement + Facilities + Security | Yes | Contract must be in place | See vendor onboarding checklist |

Entitlement lifecycle (detailed procedure):
1) Submit request: use Service Portal -> New Access Request -> include justification, expiration date, and least-privilege role selection. Attach ticket in product tracker if relevant.
2) Manager approval: approver has 72 hours to approve/deny. If no response, escalation emailed to manager's manager.
3) IAM review: IT validates mapping to SSO group and documents expected permissions. If custom role required, estimate time 3–7 business days.
4) Security gating: if Sensitive Data access requested, Security must sign-off within 5 business days or request additional controls (e.g., MFA, dedicated VPC).
5) Provisioning and verification: IT provisions access, tags entitlement with expiration, and notifies requester. Requester must confirm and log an acceptance comment.
6) Recertification: entitlements with access to Confidential or Regulated data require 90-day attestation from owner.
7) Deprovisioning: on termination or expiration, deprovision within 24 hours for contractors or 48 hours for employees.

Change management (standard & emergency):
Standard changes:
- All production-impacting changes must be submitted to the Change Board (CAB) by EOD Wednesday to be considered for the following week's window. Include risk assessment, rollback plan, and test evidence.
- SLO impact: any change expected to affect availability or latency SLOs (>=5% projected) requires pre-approval by SRE and Product.
- Communication: Release notes, status page plan, and runbook updated at least 24 hours before change.

Emergency changes:
1) Triage in incident channel and declare Emergency Change if service degradation is ongoing.
2) Emergency change owner documents: urgency reason, author, reviewers, and immediate rollback actions.
3) Post-facto CAB record: document change within 48 hours and present at next CAB for retrospective and permanent process fixes.

Data management and classification:
- Classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated.
- Default storage: all Internal+ data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Keys are managed by KMS integrations described in Security docs.
- Access to Regulated datasets requires: Data Use Agreement, contract clause, Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) completed, and storage in approved regions only.
- Retention: tables for minimum/maximum retention
| Data Type | Minimum Retention | Maximum Retention | Owner |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Audit logs | 1 year | 7 years | Security |
| Product analytics (internal) | 90 days | 3 years | Product Analytics |
| Customer PII | As required by law | Per contract | Legal |

Procurement and expense pathways:
- Methods: procurement punchout (preferred for supported SaaS), P-card (corporate card) for <= $2k one-off purchases, PO for larger spends.
- Pre-approval required for all travel and recurring SaaS subscriptions.
- Approval thresholds:
  - <= $2k: Manager approval; P-card use recommended.
  - $2k–$25k: Department Head approval plus procurement entry.
  - > $25k or multi-year: Procurement + Legal + Finance approval; formal contract and PO required.
- Competitive sourcing: required for purchases > $50k unless approved single-source exemption documented by Procurement.
- Expense reporting: receipts required for all expenses > $75. Per diem table is in the Travel Policy appendix.

Vendor onboarding & onsite requirements (checklist):
1) Contract & SOW in place and countersigned.
2) Vendor security questionnaire completed and reviewed (SOC2/ISO attestation if applicable).
3) COI (Certificate of Insurance) on file, matching contractual limits.
4) PO or vendor record created in ERP.
5) Narrowed access scope: vendors only granted access necessary for the contracted work; VPN/jump-host access approved by Security.
6) Background check required for vendors performing sensitive work (Facilities to coordinate).
7) Onsite logistics: badge registration, escorting policy (vendors without badges must be escorted at all times).
8) Emergency contact list and escalation matrix provided to Facilities and Security.

Example vendor-hosting network policy snippet (as a checklist):
- Vendor sessions must use temporary credentials with 8-hour TTL.
- All remote sessions recorded for auditing when accessing regulated assets.
- No vendor-managed software may be installed on corporate hosts without a signed Exception Request.

Travel policy highlights (for business travel):
- Pre-approval: All travel must be pre-approved in Travel Portal with itinerary and estimated costs.
- Booking: Use preferred travel vendors listed on procurement portal to leverage negotiated rates.
- Per diem & lodging: Employees should select economy/preferred class. Per diem varies by region; see Travel Rates Matrix (appendix).
- Expenses: upload itemized receipts to Expense System within 7 days of return. Cardholders must reconcile corporate card charges within 14 days monthly.
- International travel with access to customer projects: requires Security review and may require VPN split-tunnel restrictions or dedicated device.

Templates and attachments (available in Service Portal):
- Access Request Template (pre-populates required fields: justification, duration, owner): Service Portal -> Templates -> Access Request.
- Vendor Onsite Intake Form (legal/insurance checklist).
- Procurement Quick-Estimate form (for budget owners).
- Emergency Change Declaration form (to be attached to incident ticket).

Escalation and audits:
- Owners must maintain an access register for their assets. Quarterly audits are conducted by IAM and Security; findings assigned JIRA tickets with 30-day remediation SLAs.
- Procurement performs an annual vendor review for >$50k vendors, including performance, security posture, and renewal cadence.

Enforcement and exceptions:
- Exceptions: must be filed via the Risk & Exceptions process and include compensating controls, duration, and owner. Short-term operational exceptions (<=30 days) require Director-level sign-off; longer exceptions require Security Council review.

Appendix A — Quick CLI examples and automation patterns:
- Example: request access using API (curl) to the Service Portal (internal):
curl -X POST "https://service-portal.internal.redwood/api/requests" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"access","role":"data-analyst","expires_at":"2026-12-31","justification":"ad-hoc analysis for release X"}'

- Example: automated recertification reminder rule (pseudo YAML for workflow engine):
--
trigger: entitlement_expiry_approaching
condition: role in ["confidential-view", "regulated-admin"] and days_to_expiry <= 14
actions:
  - send_email: owner@redwood.com
  - create_task: IAM/recertification
--

Appendix B — Contact matrix:
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Facilities: facilities@redwood.com
- Security (access reviews): security-access@redwood.com
- IAM/IT: iam-ops@redwood.com
- Travel & Expenses: travel-expenses@redwood.com

Revision history and governance:
- This document is owned by Finance & Legal (Procurement working group) with operational stewardship by IAM and Security.
- Next major review: 2027-02-01 or after any regulatory/contractual changes.

Notes & references:
- See related: Data Residency Policy, Secure SDLC, and Vendor Risk Assessment playbooks in Security & Compliance.
- This playbook is intended to be operational — link the request or ticket IDs when raising exceptions so we keep an auditable trail.

End of document.
